text: {"question":"How does adding spatial curvature and treating the summed neutrino mass as a free parameter influence the constraints on emergent dark‑energy models that are tested with low‑redshift data?","reference_answer":"Including curvature allows the acceleration in the VC model to arise from geometry rather than dark energy, while allowing the neutrino mass to vary introduces additional degeneracies that broaden the allowed parameter space for the emergent‑DE models, making their low‑redshift signatures harder to distinguish.","passage_1_contribution":"Passage A shows that emergent‑DE models (PEDE, GEDE, GDE) rely on a hyperbolic tangent term that activates only at low redshift, and that curvature can drive acceleration in the VC case.","passage_2_contribution":"Passage B explains that the analysis treats the summed neutrino mass as a free parameter and systematically explores the impact of curvature and dynamical dark energy on cosmological constraints.","joint_reason":"Both passages discuss how adding curvature and allowing neutrino mass freedom modify the cosmological parameter space in which emergent‑DE models are constrained using low‑redshift observations.","same_quantity":false}
